response.sql: SELECT rental_totals.store_id, AVG(rental_totals.total_amount) AS avg_total_per_rental, AVG(rental_totals.payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental FROM (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(p.payment_id) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON p.rental_id = r.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id WHERE p.amount >= 4.99 GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id) AS rental_totals GROUP BY rental_totals.store_id ORDER BY rental_totals.store_id

assumptions.assumption: The '4.99 cutoff' means payments with amount >= 4.99 (inclusive threshold). A cutoff could alternatively exclude its boundary, meaning amount > 4.99.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is an exclusive boundary: keep only payments with amount > 4.99 (strictly greater than, excluding 4.99 itself)
